summary: Go SDK on Windows: socket reset causes ACK reordering and duplicate funcall executions
description: Customer reports that during high-throughput sessions from their Windows-based service, a mid-session TCP socket reset from an edge proxy causes the Go SDK streaming connection to reorder ACKs. This reordering permits the server to mark a tool/function call as unconfirmed on the reconnect path, then replay the funcall, resulting in duplicate side-effects despite the client-attached idempotency token. Occurs intermittently under burst load and correlates with recent edge-side TLS rehandshakes and a kernel-level RST from the Windows host.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Go SDK streaming client (v0.9.4) on Windows Server 2022.
2) Start a multiplexed session that issues a chain of function/tool calls (3-5 sequential funcalls) with the same per-action idempotency header.
3) Simulate short TCP RST from edge proxy (iptables or deliberate close) mid-stream on the client socket.
4) Allow client to reconnect using the same session token and resume stream.
5) Observe duplicated backend webhook/tool invocations in customer logs and missing/late ack for first run.

investigation_notes: Reproduced with minimal harness: Go SDK v0.9.4 on Windows with multiplexed sessions. On abrupt socket reset, client's reconnect path immediately pushes outstanding funcalls and relies on client-local idempotency header only. Server-side ack ledger is eventually-consistent across proxies; when ack reconciliation is delayed due to proxy rehandshake, server re-executes in-flight funcalls. Root causes: (1) SDK resume behavior that does not wait for server-confirmed last-ack when connection was reset via RST; (2) edge-proxy TLS rehandshake causing temporary split-brain view of ack ledger between proxy instances. Packet captures show client RST followed by new TCP handshake and immediate resume frames.
resolution: Deployed go-sdk v0.9.5 canary with resume handshake change: upon reconnect the client will send a resume probe and wait for explicit Last-Ack confirmation from the server before re-sending pending funcalls. Also pushed a short-term server-side dedup window (idempotency ledger TTL extended by 2 minutes for affected session types). Notified customer and monitored for 48 hours; no duplicates observed in canary traffic. Patch PRs: go-sdk PR #183 (handshake), proxy PR #44 (improved connection drain behavior).
